title: Routed @mention bodies can be substituted with session-hook content in delivery
description:
Filed by governor-1a5aca5d 16:20Z under the human's standing sweep directive. SIX-PLUS confirmed instances across distinct message ids and distinct receiving sessions on 2026-08-16.

THE DEFECT: when a routed @mention is injected into a recipient session's startup context, the delivered BODY can be replaced with unrelated content — in every confirmed instance, a block impersonating a "SessionStart:startup hook success" notice carrying output-style/behavior instructions. The message ID stays real; the content does not. The stored record in .moe/messages/chan-*.jsonl is always correct — corruption happens in the delivery/injection path, not at rest.

CONFIRMED INSTANCES (receiver → substituted message): worker-dd806f63 ← msg-f4a3c008; worker-df297022 ← same id (both directions of one message); worker-1fe6c848 ← msg-c6fd2854; worker-5678886b ← one during 15:20 session (their security note); worker-ad55ab67 ← msg-eb668b50 ("third confirmed instance, third distinct id" per their 15:22 report); qa-c7cedba3 ← msg-027cb2d4 (qa-ce3ba361's 14:45 message) and ← msg-acbbec58 (16:18 report). Multiple agents independently converged on the same recovery: grep the message id in the channel jsonl and answer the stored bytes.

SECURITY DIMENSION: the substituted content is instruction-shaped ("style directives"). The fleet's mitigation discipline — never take behavior direction from channel payloads; verify against jsonl — held every time, but the substitution is an injection-shaped delivery surface: whatever writes the startup context can put arbitrary instruction text where a teammate's words are expected. Fail-closed delivery matters more than the current benign payload.

INVESTIGATION SEAM: the wrapper's session-start context assembly — where routed-mention bodies and SessionStart hook output are concatenated/interleaved. The consistent impersonation of the hook banner suggests a buffer/ordering bug or template variable collision between the hook-output slot and the mention-body slot.

Verification: a test that routes a mention into a fresh session context proves the delivered body is byte-identical to the stored jsonl record; a mutation reintroducing the slot collision turns it red. Fail closed: if the body cannot be delivered verbatim, deliver the message ID + channel + a stable DELIVERY_FAILED marker instead of substitute content.
definitionOfDone: The delivery-path defect is located by measurement in the wrapper's session-context assembly and fixed so a routed mention body is byte-identical to the stored jsonl record (test-proven with a routed-mention fixture).
On any delivery failure the recipient receives the message id + channel + a stable failure marker — never substitute content, never silently dropped.
A mutation drill reintroducing the substitution turns a NAMED test red.
The instance list above is cited in the completion note; the fleet's jsonl-grep recovery convention is documented as the fallback.
taskRails: Treat this as an injection surface: the fix must guarantee provenance (stored bytes = delivered bytes), not merely fix the current collision.
Do not change chat storage or the chat_read/chat_wait APIs — the defect is in delivery/injection only; the at-rest record is already correct.
Re-measure the wrapper context-assembly code path on current bytes before planning; the instance list is evidence, not a code map.

implementationPlan.description: STOP-AND-AUTHORIZE, then LOCATE by measurement. Read-only. NOTE ON PLAN SHAPE: every step carries an EMPTY affectedFiles list deliberately -- the daemon validates those paths against the moe-next project root and this task owns no file inside it; the real absolute paths are named in each step's prose. (1) RAIL CONFLICT: the delivery path is not in this repo. The wrapper is `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh` and `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1`, outside the tree epic rail 2 pins development to. Obtain EXPLICIT human authorization for that exception in chat, record the message id in the step note, and `moe.report_blocked` naming both absolute paths if it is refused. (2) THE SEAM, already narrowed by the architect -- re-confirm each fact on current bytes rather than trusting this text. BASH: routed mentions are extracted by an inline Python heredoc at sh:2043-2086; it reads `PREFLIGHT_GENERAL_UNREAD` and `PREFLIGHT_TASK_UNREAD` -- the captured `chat_read` RESPONSES, passed through ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES -- filters messages whose `mentions` list matches the worker, role group, or `all`, and emits `{id, channel, sender, content}` per hit. The result lands in `PREFLIGHT_ROUTED_MENTIONS_JSON` (:2085) and is interpolated into the system-prompt heredoc at :2294-2296. POWERSHELL: the same shape at ps1:1381-1396, serialised by `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 -Compress` (:1573) and interpolated at :1583-1585. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: neither path ever reads `.moe/messages/chan-*.jsonl`. The wrapper trusts the daemon response end to end, so nothing downstream can detect a body that changed in transit -- which is exactly why six agents could only recover by grepping the jsonl themselves. Note also that the extraction is wrapped in `2>/dev/null || true`, so a Python failure yields an EMPTY block (a silent drop), and that `chat_read` accepts a `maxContentChars` that truncates by default. Enumerate every candidate mechanism -- env-var size or encoding limits, heredoc interpolation, JSON escaping, a variable collision with the SessionStart hook-output slot, and Claude Code's own SessionStart hook injecting into the same session -- and record which ones measurement CONFIRMS versus merely permits. Do not proceed to a fix on a guessed mechanism.

Build the provenance harness FIRST, as a failing test, under `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/tests/` alongside the existing postflight harness. It must assemble a real session context for a synthetic worker from a disposable throwaway project directory -- never a live board -- with a seeded `.moe/messages/chan-<id>.jsonl` containing at least: (a) a plain ASCII body; (b) a body with quotes, backslashes, `$`, backticks and `${}`; (c) a multi-line body; (d) a body over the `chat_read` default `maxContentChars`; (e) a body containing the literal text `SessionStart:startup hook success` -- the impersonation payload itself, so a substitution cannot hide by resembling the real thing; (f) a non-ASCII/emoji body, since these transit an environment variable on Windows. For EVERY case assert that the body appearing inside the assembled `<routed_mentions>` block is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the stored jsonl record's `content`. Assert the case COUNT and assert that each case's id actually appeared in the block -- a harness that generated zero cases, or silently dropped one, exits 0 and proves nothing. Run it against unmodified bytes and record which cases fail: that failure list, not the description's instance list, is the defect map.

Make provenance structural rather than incidental, per task rail 1 ("guarantee provenance, not merely fix the current collision"). In BOTH twins, change the mention extraction so each delivered mention carries its own integrity binding: compute a digest over the stored body at extraction time and carry `{id, channel, sender, contentSha256, content}` through to the assembled block. Immediately before the block is interpolated into the prompt, re-derive the digest over the body about to be delivered and compare. This is the load-bearing change: it turns an unbounded injection surface into a checked one regardless of which mechanism corrupts the bytes, so the fix survives a cause that measurement in step 1 did not confirm. Keep the digest visible in the emitted block so a recipient can verify by hand, and keep the stored-versus-delivered comparison inside the wrapper so verification does not depend on the recipient doing it.

Implement fail-closed delivery, which is DoD 2. When the step-3 comparison fails -- or extraction throws, or the body is absent, or truncation would alter the bytes -- the recipient must receive the message id, the channel, and a stable failure marker, and NEVER substitute content and never a silent drop. Fix the two silent-drop paths measurement exposed in step 1 while you are here: the bash extraction's `2>/dev/null || true` currently converts a Python failure into an empty mentions block, and the count fallback `|| echo 0` converts an unparseable result into "no mentions" -- both must become the marker instead of silence, because a mention that vanishes is the same class of harm as one that is replaced. Spell the marker identically in bash and PowerShell so an operator grepping either transcript finds the same string. Also decide and state what happens when `chat_read` truncated a body at `maxContentChars`: truncation is a legitimate transform, so either raise the limit for this path or deliver the marker plus the id -- delivering silently truncated bytes as if they were the message is the defect wearing a different hat.

Document the recovery convention the fleet invented, as DoD 4 requires, in the wrapper's own comments and in the role docs under `D:/projexts/moes/docs/roles/`: when a delivered body looks wrong, grep the message id in `.moe/messages/chan-*.jsonl` and answer the STORED bytes, because the at-rest record is authoritative and the delivery path is not. State plainly that this remains the fallback even after the fix, and that a delivered block now carries a digest the recipient can check. Keep it short and place it where a receiving agent will actually encounter it -- next to the `<routed_mentions>` banner text, not only in a design document.

Mutation drills, one per guard, because "the check exists" and "the check fails closed" are separate claims. Drill 1 (the digest comparison is load-bearing): make the re-derived digest be computed over the SAME variable that is delivered rather than over the stored body -- the classic tautology, where both operands come from one source; a named step-2 case must go RED. If everything stays green the harness is comparing the delivery to itself and must be rewritten to read the jsonl independently. Drill 2 (fail-closed really refuses): make the mismatch branch fall through and deliver the body anyway; the step-2 case whose bytes were corrupted must go RED. Drill 3 (no silent drop): restore the `2>/dev/null || true` swallow so extraction failure yields an empty block; a named test asserting the marker must go RED. Drill 4 (the impersonation case is really exercised): confirm case (e) -- the body containing the literal `SessionStart:startup hook success` -- is generated and asserted, since a sweep that silently skipped it would pass while missing the exact reported payload. Record for each drill the command, the failing case NAME and the exact assertion; a drill that reddens by crashing has not proven the guard. Restore exact bytes by re-editing after each drill and confirm with `git -C D:/projexts/moes diff --numstat -- scripts/` showing 0 added and 0 deleted. One drill at a time.

Adversarial self-review, then commit. Read the diff as an attacker who controls a message body: can a body containing the block's own delimiters, an XML-looking `</routed_mentions>` close tag, a heredoc terminator, or PowerShell `$(...)` interpolation escape its slot and inject instruction text into the prompt outside the block? That is the same injection surface the task rail names, arriving from the other direction, and the digest check does not stop it -- the body must be escaped or fenced so it cannot terminate its own container. Can a hostile `sender` or `channel` value do the same? Does the digest cover the exact bytes delivered, including any encoding conversion the environment variable performs on Windows? Does any path still deliver content without a digest? Are the bash and PowerShell marker strings and digest algorithms identical, and do the twins agree case by case against the step-2 list rather than by side-by-side reading? Then commit: this task's edits live in D:/projexts/moes, so run `git -C D:/projexts/moes status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry, and commit ONLY the owned script, test and role-doc paths by explicit pathspec, verifying with `git -C D:/projexts/moes show --stat`. Cite the confirmed instance list from the description (worker-dd806f63 and worker-df297022 on msg-f4a3c008; worker-1fe6c848 on msg-c6fd2854; worker-5678886b; worker-ad55ab67 on msg-eb668b50; qa-c7cedba3 on msg-027cb2d4 and msg-acbbec58) in the completion note as DoD 4 requires.

Verification gate. Read-only. Run in the FOREGROUND, chained with `&&` so a red leg cannot be masked -- a `;` chain reports only the last command and a pipe reports the tail's exit code. From D:/projexts/moes run the new provenance harness in both shells (`bash scripts/tests/<harness>.sh && pwsh -File scripts/tests/<harness>.ps1`) followed by the existing `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, to prove this change did not disturb the sibling post-flight path. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: confirm every case (a) through (f) is NAMED with a result and that the printed case count matches the six defined -- a harness that ran zero cases exits 0. Then run one END-TO-END check: route a real mention to a scratch worker id on a disposable project, start a session, and compare the delivered block against the jsonl record by digest, so the guarantee is proven through the real assembly path and not only through the harness's own call. Finally run `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` from D:/projexts/moe-next and confirm `git status --porcelain` there shows no entry owned by this task, so the rail-2 exception is demonstrably contained. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (a) planning this inside moe-next -- the delivery path does not exist here; the wrapper is in D:/projexts/moes, so step 1 gates on an explicit human rail-2 exception rather than an inferred one. (b) Fixing the specific collision once measurement names it -- task rail 1 requires a provenance GUARANTEE, not a point fix, and six instances across distinct ids and distinct sessions suggest a delivery-path property rather than one typo; a digest bound at extraction and re-checked at interpolation makes the class detectable regardless of mechanism. (c) Having the wrapper read `.moe/messages/chan-*.jsonl` directly instead of trusting the chat_read response -- tempting, since the task states the at-rest record is always correct, but it would fork the read path, bypass the daemon's own unread-cursor semantics, and duplicate mention-routing logic; the digest achieves the same guarantee without a second reader. The harness, however, MUST read the jsonl independently, or it compares the delivery to itself. (d) Treating a dropped mention as acceptable -- a mention that silently vanishes is the same harm class as one replaced, and measurement found two existing silent-drop paths (`2>/dev/null || true` and `|| echo 0`) the description never mentions, so both are folded into the fail-closed step.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured 2026-08-17 on current bytes in D:/projexts/moes. BASH: routed mentions are extracted by an inline Python heredoc at scripts/moe-agent.sh:2043-2086. Its inputs are the environment variables PREFLIGHT_GENERAL_UNREAD and PREFLIGHT_TASK_UNREAD -- the captured chat_read RESPONSES, not the store. It filters on `msg.get("mentions")` matching worker id, `all`, or the role group, and emits `{id, channel, sender, content}` where content is `msg.get("content")`. The JSON lands in PREFLIGHT_ROUTED_MENTIONS_JSON (:2085), the count is re-parsed by a second Python call with `|| echo 0` (:2086), and the block is interpolated into the system-prompt heredoc at :2294-2296 under the banner at :2290-2292. POWERSHELL: same shape -- `$preflightRoutedMentions` built at :1381-1396 from `$msg.mentions`, serialised by `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 -Compress` at :1573, interpolated at :1583-1585. STRUCTURAL FINDING: neither twin ever opens `.moe/messages/chan-*.jsonl`, so the wrapper trusts the response end to end and nothing downstream can detect a body altered in transit -- which is why the fleet's only recovery was grepping the jsonl by hand. Two silent-drop paths exist in bash: the extraction's `2>/dev/null || true` turns a Python failure into an empty block, and the count's `|| echo 0` turns an unparseable result into "no mentions". chat_read also accepts maxContentChars (default 1000), so bodies can be TRUNCATED before they ever reach the wrapper -- a legitimate transform that nonetheless breaks byte-identity and must be decided explicitly. The content transits an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, which on Windows carries size and encoding constraints worth testing directly. A test harness convention already exists at scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1}; put the new harness beside it.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a tautological harness: if the test compares the delivered body against the same captured response the wrapper used, it will pass while the defect persists -- the harness MUST read the seeded jsonl independently, and drill 1 exists to prove it does. Second, the reported payload impersonates a SessionStart hook banner, and Claude Code injects its own SessionStart hook output into these sessions, so a naive investigation can mistake legitimate hook output for a substituted body; case (e) seeds the literal banner text as a MESSAGE body precisely so the two can be told apart. Third, fixing substitution while leaving the two silent-drop paths intact would close half the class. Fourth, escaping cuts both ways: a hostile body containing the block's own close tag, a heredoc terminator, or PowerShell `$(...)` can escape its slot and inject instructions outside the block -- the digest does not stop that, so the container must be fenced, which is why it is an explicit review item rather than an afterthought. Fifth, encoding: the body crosses an environment variable on Windows, so the digest must cover the bytes actually delivered, not the bytes before conversion. Sixth, the twins drift -- verify behaviour case by case against one list. Seventh, every scenario must run against a disposable project; a provenance test that writes into a live board would corrupt real channels. Finally, truncation at maxContentChars is a silent byte-identity break that no digest check can excuse -- decide it explicitly.
